data_sources.name: ACS PUMS 2014-2018 5-year, household and person files
data_sources.how: Download csv_h<st>.zip and csv_p<st>.zip for st = dc, de, md, pa, va, wv from the 2018 5-Year folder (CSV, not SAS). Variables used: SERIALNO, ST, PUMA, MIGPUMA, MIGSP, POWPUMA, POWSP, MIG, MV, RELP, AGEP, ESR, JWMNP, SCHG, NP, TYPE, BDSP, BLD, TEN, GRNTP, SMOCP, VALP, HINCP, VEH, YBL, WGTP; ADJINC (income adjustment) and ADJHSG (housing-cost adjustment) are columns of the same files.
notes: URL: the folder of the documented 2019 and 2024 5-Year files (2_silo/data_sources.md) with the year 2018: verify.
The package copy is 00_shared_data/acs_pums_2014_2018_5yr/ (project: ../inputs/pums_2018_5yr/). The package scripts read the package copy; replace its files by your download.

data_sources.name: MSTM zone system, zone polygons and peak car skim (Maryland Statewide Transportation Model)
data_sources.provider: Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration (MDOT SHA), provided to the project
data_sources.how: Not a public download: the 1,588-zone MSTM system (zoneSystem.csv), zone polygons (SMZ_RMZ_02152011inMSTM_EPSG26918.shp) and the AM-peak auto travel-time skim were provided by MDOT. Request them from MDOT SHA (MSTM / travel forecasting).
notes: verify: landing page only; the data are MDOT-provided.

Project copies: 2_silo/input/zoneSystem.csv, ../ABIT/input/mito_los/Zonal/*.shp, 2_silo/input/skims/auto_peak_time.csv.gz; package copies in 00_shared_data/zone_system and 00_shared_data/skims (used by the package scripts).

data_sources.name: CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items (annual averages 2014-2023)
data_sources.how: Series CUUR0000SA0, annual averages; the values are typed in rc.py (CPI dict) and used to express incomes in 2016 dollars.
notes: verify: landing page of the series; no file is read (constants in rc.py).

data_sources.name: Regional Travel Survey 2017/18 (household, person, trip records)
data_sources.provider: Baltimore Metropolitan Council (BMC) and National Capital Region Transportation Planning Board (TPB/MWCOG)
data_sources.how: Restricted: request the 2017/2018 Regional Travel Survey data from BMC / TPB. File used: RTS_raw_flat_data.csv (flat person-level file with household fields: household_id, person_id, home_state_county_fips, home_tract_fips, home_type, hhsize, numvehicle, numdrivers, hh_income_detailed, wthhfin, wtperfin, age, age_group, employment_status, j1_workplace_loc, work_state_county_fips, work_tract_fips, license, school locations and BMC/TPB TAZ codes). Also rts_trips_clean.csv (cleaned trips) for the synthetic-population workplace step.
notes: verify: landing page only; restricted data.

Project location: ../ABIT/input/rts/. Package copy: 00_shared_data/rts_2017_18/ (with rts_split.csv, the project's random 50/50 household split, and tract_zone.csv, the tract-to-zone table of 3_abit/survey_pop).

data_sources.name: LEHD LODES 8, Workplace Area Characteristics 2016 and geography crosswalk, Maryland
data_sources.how: Download md_wac_S000_JT00_2016.csv.gz and https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/LODES8/md/md_xwalk.csv.gz (other states: .../LODES8/<st>/wac/<st>_wac_S000_JT00_<year>.csv.gz). files: <st>_wac_S000_JT00_2017.csv.gz (st = md, dc, va, pa, de, wv)

steps.what: Household table hh.parquet from PUMS Maryland (package copy; overwrites input/data/raw/hh.parquet)
input_check, part 1: keep a copy of the provided estimation and hold-out tables
steps.command: rm -rf provided_estimation provided_holdout && cp -R estimation provided_estimation && cp -R holdout provided_holdout

steps.what: Build the estimation and hold-out tables from the inputs (same calls and random draws as the original run; adds the persons-16+ dummies and the Baltimore City column)
input_check, part 2: compare the rebuilt tables with the provided ones (rows, column sums, largest difference); must print ALL TABLES MATCH
Log-likelihood at the article coefficients (no estimation, nothing written)
Biogeme estimation, start values = article estimates
Compare the estimates with the article (reference_estimates.csv)

notes: Age = age of the oldest member (as the engine computes it), (age - 45)/10 and its square.
ln income x ln density uses the density centred at the estimation-sample mean 5.485957407613654 (already in the column).

Persons aged 16+ (workers + nonworking_adults) enter as dummies for 2, 3 and 4+ (reference 0-1); nonworking_adults is not in the model. Baltimore City (PUMA 2400801-2400805) has its own term, estimated with the other coefficients.
Fixed at 0 (p > 0.3 when estimated): single person for 2 and 3+ cars, ln density for 1 car, age for 3+ cars; 56 parameters.
Steps with output_provided = true can be skipped: their results are in input/data or 00_shared_data. Upstream project stages were not re-run for this package; their runtimes are not measured.

Measured here: --check 4 s, 0.8 GB; estimation a few seconds (coefficients and robust s.e. equal to the article's to 4 decimals). Remove or rename an old output/__car_ownership.iter before estimating: Biogeme starts from it.
Environment: Biogeme scripts and package build scripts run with ~/.venvs/biogeme/bin/python (Biogeme 3.3.5); project scripts with /opt/homebrew/anaconda3/bin/python3 (needs geopandas).
